name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), a benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks, 58 datasets, and 112 languages, with open-source code and a public leaderboard.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
citeAs: Muennighoff, Niklas; Tazi, Nouamane; Magne, Loïc; Reimers, Nils. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3 [cs.CL], 19 Mar 2023.
rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies 58 datasets from 8 embedding tasks: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. Datasets are sourced from existing benchmarks such as SemEval STS and BEIR, uploaded via Hugging Face dataset names, and some datasets are custom-made for MTEB. The paper states that ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering and MedrxivClustering were custom-made for MTEB using the public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv. RedditClusteringP2P and StackExchangeClusteringP2P were created for MTEB using available Reddit and StackExchange post data.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data come from 58 constituent datasets across 8 tasks. Sources explicitly mentioned include SemEval STS datasets, BEIR datasets, Hugging Face datasets, public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, available Reddit posts, available StackExchange posts, Kaggle competition datasets, Amazon reviews, Twitter messages, AskUbuntu questions, Stack Overflow questions, Tatoeba sentence pairs, BUCC comparable corpora, and SummEval summaries.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For clustering datasets custom-made for MTEB, S2S inputs use only paper titles, while P2P inputs concatenate title and abstract. For arXiv, when multiple categories can be given to a paper, only the first category is used. For every clustering dataset, split and strategy, subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels. MTEB also groups datasets into sentence-to-sentence, paragraph-to-paragraph, and sentence-to-paragraph categories.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Implementation details include task-specific processing. For classification, train and test sets are embedded and a logistic regression classifier with 100 maximum iterations is trained on train embeddings and scored on test embeddings. For clustering, embedded texts are clustered with mini-batch k-means with batch size 32 and k equal to the number of labels. For pair classification and STS, texts are embedded and distances computed with metrics such as cosine similarity, dot product, euclidean distance, and manhattan distance. For retrieval and reranking, queries and documents/references are embedded and compared using cosine similarity. For summarization, machine and human summaries are embedded and the closest human-summary score is kept. The paper also states that evaluations are run on the test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO, where the dev split is used.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are inherited from the underlying datasets and, for some custom MTEB datasets, created from existing human-provided metadata. Examples explicitly stated include: clustering labels for arXiv, bioRxiv and medRxiv are generated using categories given to the papers by humans; BUCC and Tatoeba provide associated pairs corresponding to translated sentence pairs; AskUbuntu has manual annotations marking pairs of questions as similar or dissimilar; SummEval includes human annotations of machine-generated summaries; STS datasets use continuous similarity scores; classification datasets use labels such as polarity, intent, emotion, toxicity, or sentiment from their source datasets.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For pair classification, the best binary threshold is selected and metrics are computed. For clustering, v-measure is used and does not depend on cluster label permutation. For STS and summarization, Pearson and Spearman correlations with ground truth labels or human assessments are computed, with Spearman correlation based on cosine similarity serving as the main metric. The paper does not describe annotator disagreement analysis.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB aims for reproducibility through versioning at a dataset and software level. JSON files corresponding to all results in the paper have been made available together with the benchmark on the Hugging Face Hub. The benchmark provides open-source software, a public leaderboard, and welcomes dataset, task, or metric contributions from the community via pull requests and leaderboard additions via an automatic submission format.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes datasets containing language information across 112 languages and multilingual datasets. Some constituent datasets explicitly involve user-generated text and potentially sensitive content, such as online banking queries, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter messages, toxic comments from the Civil Comments platform, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, and medical or biomedical text. Specific sensitive attributes collected are not summarized centrally in the paper.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research and industry applications. The paper discusses that current narrow evaluation leads to the blind application of models to new use cases in industry, and MTEB aims to provide clarity on model performance across varied use cases.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes task imbalance in MTEB: summarization has only a single dataset, so average scores are biased toward tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering. It also notes that retrieval and clustering are English-only, limiting multilingual evaluation. The authors state that controlling for overlap between MTEB datasets and model training datasets is challenging and that they ignore overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets in MTEB scores.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper lists several limitations: long document datasets are missing, with the longest datasets having only a few hundred words; tasks are imbalanced, with some tasks underrepresented such as summarization and pair classification; multilingual coverage is incomplete because retrieval and clustering are English-only and there are no code datasets; and the benchmark focuses solely on natural language applications and not additional modalities such as image content. The paper also notes that data contamination between benchmark datasets and model training data is challenging to control.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluation and benchmarking of text embedding models across 8 tasks and 58 datasets, including model comparison, leaderboard reporting, and establishing baselines. It is used on train/test splits for classification and on test splits of datasets for evaluation, except MSMARCO where the dev split is used. The benchmark is intended to support future research and industry model selection rather than model training itself.
